name: Quantum Blur
description: Apply a quantum blur algorithm to the image.

input_files.name: image
input_files.description: The image of your choice. The blur effect is applied RGB pixel values only, not the alpha channel. It means that if you submitted a PNG with transparent background, the background from the output will also be transparent.

input_files.name: mask
input_files.description:
Optional mask controlling where the effect is applied, on a per-pixel
basis. Must match the size of `image`. Each output pixel is a soft
blend `C = m · C_blurred + (1 - m) · C_original`, where `m` is the
normalised mask intensity at that pixel: black keeps the original,
white takes the fully blurred version, and grey values blend smoothly
between the two. Single-channel masks are used directly; RGB masks are
converted to luminance.

**Alpha-channel fallback**

If no mask is provided, the alpha channel of `image` is used instead
(transparent pixels keep the original, opaque pixels are blurred). For
RGB input with no alpha channel, the whole image is blurred.

downscale.description:
Strategy used when a mask region is larger than the maximum number of qubits allows:

- `true` — the region is downscaled to fit, blurred, and upscaled back.
- `false` — the region is split into adjacent tiles that are blurred independently.
downscale.title: Downscale

reach.description:
Controls how far from its original position a pixel can be affected by the blur:

- `0` — fully local: only nearby pixels are affected (default).
- `1` — fully non-local: pixels anywhere on the canvas can be affected equally.
reach.title: Reach

size.description: Pixel budget per blur pass: a region up to `size × size` pixels is blurred in a single pass. Internally converted to a qubit budget via `ceil(log2(size)) * 2`. Must be between 8 and 1024. Default 1024.
size.title: Size

strength.description:
Strength of the effect, which controls the rotation applied to each qubit:

- `0` — the image is left unchanged.
- `1` — maximum blur.
strength.title: Strength

style.description:
Quantum gate used to apply the effect:

- `rx` — rotation around the x-axis of the Bloch sphere.
- `ry` — rotation around the y-axis of the Bloch sphere.
style.title: Style

description_md:
A unitary, information-preserving blur driven by quantum interference.

Instead of averaging each pixel with its neighbours, Quantum Blur scatters
every part of the image across every other part at once. The result looks less
like a classical soft focus and more like a fractal echo, where shapes from
one corner reappear, faintly and rearranged, across the rest of the canvas.
The effect is applied only inside the region selected by the `mask` (or the
alpha channel when no mask is given).

### How to use

Invoke the engine through the platform with a JSON params payload and one or
two image files attached:

- `image` — required. The source image. Supported formats: PNG, JPEG, WebP,
  TIFF, BMP.
- `mask` — optional. A single-channel (or RGB) image the same size as `image`,
  where brighter pixels receive more of the blurred result and darker pixels
  keep the original. If omitted, the alpha channel of `image` is used as the
  mask; for RGB input with no alpha, the whole image is blurred.

Optionally, the params object may also include:

- `strength` — strength of the blur. Default `0.5`.
- `style` — quantum gate used to apply the blur. Default `"rx"`.
- `downscale` — strategy for regions larger than `size` allows. Default `True`.
- `size` — pixel budget per blur pass: a region up to `size × size` pixels is
  blurred in a single pass. Must be between 8 and 1024. Default `1024`.
- `reach` — how far from its original position a pixel can be affected by the
  blur. `0` is fully local (default); `1` is maximally non-local. Default `0.0`.

### Output

Returns the blurred image in the same format and dimensions as the input. The
original alpha channel, if any, is preserved unchanged.

code_samples.source:
import requests

with open("image.png", "rb") as img:
    r = requests.post(
        "https://api.mothquantum.com/v1/generation/blur-v1/process",
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_KEY"},
        files={"image": img},
        data={"strength": 0.5, "style": "rx", "non_locality": 0.0},
    )
job = r.json()
print(job["job_id"])

import requests

with open("image.png", "rb") as img, open("mask.png", "rb") as msk:
    r = requests.post(
        "https://api.mothquantum.com/v1/generation/blur-v1/process",
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_KEY"},
        files={"image": img, "mask": msk},
        data={"strength": 0.7},
    )
job = r.json()
print(job["job_id"])
